statement: The Despotate of Epirus and the Empire of Nicaea were the two main claimants to Byzantine imperial legitimacy after the Fourth Crusade (1204). Theodore Komnenos Doukas of Epirus captured Thessalonica (1224) and proclaimed himself Emperor — directly challenging Nicaea's Theodore I Laskaris. The rivalry between the two 'Byzantine' claimants, sometimes violent, weakened both against the Latin Empire and later against the Bulgarians (Theodore was captured by Tsar Ivan Asen II at Klokotnitsa, 1230). Nicaea eventually prevailed, retaking Constantinople in 1261.
